detail.title: Commercial Counsel
detail.jobDescription:
The Role

We're hiring our first in-house commercial counsel to own the legal side of deal execution. This is not a compliance or governance role — it's a deal acceleration role.

You'll own the full contract lifecycle — MSA, DPA, Order Forms, security addenda, and customer redlines — and build the playbook that lets the majority of deals close without legal intervention at all.


What You'll Do


• Own all commercial contract negotiation and execution — MSAs, DPAs, Order Forms, amendments, renewals
• Review and turn customer redlines in hours, not days
• Build and maintain a contract playbook — pre-approved fallback positions, self-serve templates for SMB/MM, approved language library
• Work directly with the sales team — you'll know which deals are strategic and which redlines matter
• Manage outside counsel for complex or novel matters — international compliance, regulatory, M&A-adjacent terms
• Own Japan APPI compliance and addenda for our growing JP enterprise business
• Partner with Customer Success on renewal and expansion contract terms
• Build scalable legal processes so SMB/MM self-serves where possible, while Enterprise gets faster, cleaner turns.


What We're Looking For


• 7-12 years of experience in commercial/transactional law, ideally at a high-growth enterprise SaaS, experienced in series rounds and/or IPO.
• Deep experience with enterprise MSAs, DPAs, data privacy frameworks (GDPR, CCPA, APPI), and security addenda
• Has built a contract playbook before — you know how to turn bespoke legal work into repeatable, scalable processes
• Comfortable working embedded in a sales team, not in a legal silo. You attend pipeline reviews, you know deal context, you move fast.
• Experience managing outside counsel relationships — know when to escalate vs. handle in-house
• SOC 2, ISO 27001 environment experience preferred
• International experience strongly preferred — EMEA (GDPR) and APJ (especially Japan APPI). We have a significant and growing enterprise business in Japan, with EMEA expansion ahead.
• Bar admission in at least one US state preferred.

About Genspark

Genspark.ai is a Palo Alto, CA-based technology company building agentic AI for more than one billion global knowledge workers. Founded by veterans from Microsoft, Google, Meta, YouTube, and Pinterest, Genspark has raised $645 million from investors including Emergence Capital Partners, LG, SBI, UpHonest, and Temasek’s Pavilion Capital. Genspark orchestrates 70+ state-of-the-art AI models to turn business objectives into finished deliverables, including boardroom presentations, financial models, client-ready documents, full-stack web applications, mobile apps, and more. Empowered by partnerships with OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Microsoft, and many other industry leaders, Genspark serves both individual users and enterprise clients worldwide. Built for every knowledge worker, whether leading a team or just starting their career. Learn more at genspark.ai.

We're scaling our enterprise go-to-market from 7 AEs to 55+ across the US and Japan through 2026 and expanding into EMEA. That means a tremendous number of enterprise deals per year, a growing international footprint, and a legal function that needs to be built from the ground up.

Compensation & Benefits:

The base salary range for this role is $200,000 – $275,000. In addition to base salary, this role is also eligible to receive and/or earn a discretionary bonus, based on Company's plans and in accordance with Company's policies. In addition to base salary, the role includes the opportunity to receive equity and a full range of benefits, including comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, flexible PTO, and 401(k).

Final compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's skills, experience, and qualifications and will be determined during the interview process. Ranges for candidates in other locations may differ based on cost of labor and other factors for those locations.

Equal Opportunity

detail.title: Solutions Engineer
detail.jobDescription:
This is the first technical seller in the GTM org and the person who defines what world-class SE looks like at Genspark. You'll sit across the table from sophisticated IT and security buyers who test every claim we make. Your job is to earn their trust, prove the platform, and win the technical decision.

Because you're first, you're not inheriting a playbook — you're writing it. You'll partner directly with our GTM leaders and Account Executives, shape how we demo and run technical evaluations, and build the foundation the next ten SEs will use.

This role reports to the Head of GTM Engineering (Eduardo Ynaty) — flat org, no layers between you and the decision-maker.

What You'll Do

- Run the technical sales motion end-to-end — discovery, architecture, demos, whiteboard sessions, executive briefings, and the security review that wins technical buy-in.

- Go deep on the prospect's stack — identity providers, CRMs, ITSM, cloud infrastructure, and the SaaS apps Genspark integrates with. Scope integrations, anticipate blockers, and prove value in a pilot.

- Translate technical environments into scoped pilots — define success criteria, build proof-of-concept workspaces, and demonstrate how Genspark's multi-agent workflows replace point-tool sprawl.

- Be the credible voice on security and access — fluent in guardrails, approval workflows, least-privilege access, audit logging, and the compliance questions security teams actually press on. No hand-waving.

- Build the SE toolkit from scratch — demo environments, reference architectures, evaluation frameworks, technical FAQs, competitive positioning, and repeatable plays that scale the team.

- Act as the bridge between field and product — capture the hardest objections, feature gaps, and real-world use cases, then work directly with Engineering to close them.

- Enable the broader GTM org — package what you learn into demo assets, talk tracks, and training that makes AEs and future SEs better.

Who You Are

- 5+ years in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or a comparable pre-sales technical role at a B2B software or infrastructure company.

- A builder at heart — you can scope what matters, stand up a demo or proof-of-value yourself, and ship it. You don't wait for someone else to build the deck.

- Deeply technical and credible — the kind of person who earns the respect of CIOs, Heads of IT, and security leaders in the first meeting. You can hold your own in an architecture review, debug an integration live, and answer a sharp security question without reaching for a slide.

- AI-fluent, not AI-bullish — you understand how LLMs, agentic workflows, and multi-modal AI systems actually work in enterprise contexts. You can explain the difference between a deterministic script and a reasoning agent — and why that matters for a security review.

- A trusted advisor by instinct — you listen for the real problem and prove value in the sales cycle rather than pitching features.

- Comfortable in ambiguity — you own your work end-to-end, move without waiting to be told what to build next, and know that "first SE" means writing the FAQ, not reading it.

- Excellent communicator — you can translate a complex multi-agent workflow into clear business value for a CFO, then switch to technical depth for an engineering reviewer. You write clearly and present persuasively.

Nice to Have

- Programming fluency (Python, JavaScript, or SQL) — enough to wire APIs, build a quick demo, or debug a prototype.

- Experience with enterprise security, compliance, and procurement processes (RFPs, DPAs, risk assessments, SSO/SCIM).

- Prior founding or early-stage SE experience — you've been the first SE before and know what it takes.

- Familiarity with the modern IT stack: IdPs, SCIM, ITSM, CRM, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise SaaS administration.

- GTM Engineering or Forward Deployed Engineering exposure — you understand the builder/seller hybrid model.

Location

Remote-friendly across the US. Preference for NYC and Palo Alto — we have a small Palo Alto office (engineering + cofounding team) and a NYC office is likely coming. Everyone outside Palo Alto is currently remote.

Equal Opportunity

Genspark is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

detail.title: Head of B2B Marketing
detail.jobDescription:
The Opportunity

Genspark is at an inflection point. We built an AI workspace that 1B+ knowledge workers actually want to use. In 10 months, we went from 0 to $155M ARR—the fastest growth in the agent space. We launched Genspark for Business (Team and Enterprise plans) in November 2025, and over 6,000 organizations have already onboarded.

But here's the thing: we've barely scratched the surface of our B2B potential.

The next growth unlock is converting this organic product pull into a repeatable enterprise revenue engine. That's where you come in.

We're looking for a Head of B2B Marketing to build the bridge from our bottoms-up product adoption to top-down enterprise pipeline and revenue. This is not a "run the playbook" role. This is a "define the playbook" role. You'll be the first dedicated B2B marketing leader, with a seat at the leadership table, the opportunity to bring in your best folks, and ownership over how we take Genspark to market with mid-market and enterprise customers.

What You'll Own

The B2B Marketing Function (0→1)

  • Build the B2B marketing function from the ground up—strategy, team, systems, and culture

  • Define the enterprise narrative and segmentation strategy for Team and Enterprise plans

  • Own the full-funnel B2B marketing motion from awareness through pipeline to expansion

  • Establish the operating rhythm with Sales, Product, and Growth teams

PLG-to-Enterprise Bridge

  • Design the motion that converts product-qualified accounts (PQAs) into enterprise pipeline

  • Build the infrastructure to translate product usage signals into sales-ready opportunities

  • Create the case study and proof engine that gives enterprise buyers confidence

Go-to-Market Strategy

  • Partner with Sales Leadership as the primary marketing strategist and advisor

  • Shape pricing, packaging, and positioning for B2B tiers

  • Design and execute ABM, field marketing, and demand generation programs

  • Build the events and executive briefing strategy that moves markets, not just fills calendars

Revenue Impact

  • Own pipeline creation and acceleration targets for B2B segments

  • Build measurement frameworks that prove marketing's contribution to revenue

  • Influence how the company thinks about attribution, investment, and GTM priorities

  • Report directly to the C-suite on B2B marketing performance and strategic initiatives

What You've Done Before

  • 12–15 years in B2B marketing, with at least 5 years in a leadership role at a high-growth SaaS company

  • Direct experience building or significantly contributing to a B2B marketing function at a product-led company moving from self-serve to sales-assisted/enterprise

  • Deep fluency in demand generation, ABM, field marketing, and revenue marketing—plus the ability to move between strategy and hands-on execution

  • Proven track record building pipeline, accelerating deals, and influencing revenue in B2B segments

  • Strong cross-functional leadership with Sales, Product, and Growth teams—you know how to earn trust and drive alignment

  • Comfort with ambiguity and early-stage motion building—you're energized by 0→1, not intimidated by it

  • Executive presence and credibility to present to C-suite stakeholders and challenge assumptions with data

What Will Make You Successful Here

  • You bridge worlds. You can translate product usage data into enterprise sales narratives. You speak both "bottoms-up adoption" and "top-down procurement."

  • You build systems. You're not just running campaigns—you're building the infrastructure that makes B2B marketing repeatable and scalable.

  • You move fast. We're a company that went from 0 to $155M ARR in 10 months. We need someone who can keep pace and build while the plane is flying.

  • You think in revenue. You understand that marketing's job is to create and accelerate pipeline, not just generate activity.

  • You're a strategic partner. You don't just take direction from sales—you help shape the GTM strategy alongside sales leadership.

About Genspark

Built for every knowledge worker, whether leading a team or just starting their career. Learn more at genspark.ai.

detail.title: Account Executive, Mid-Market (Commercial Sales)
detail.jobDescription:
About Genspark

Genspark is doing $250M ARR after a year, and we just closed $400M in new funding. Customers are coming faster than we can staff to meet them.

Why? Instead of building on one AI model, we plug into 70+ and let the system pick the right one for the job. Better answers on more kinds of work, no lock-in to any single lab, and the bill can land a lot lower than running everything through one frontier model. In a world where CFOs are now pushing on the ROI of AI spend, that last point matters a lot.

And Genspark is not just one product. It's seven:

  • Genspark is the AI workspace: research, docs, slides, design, code, all in one place.

  • GenMail takes over your inbox: drafts in your voice, briefs you every morning, gets you to zero faster.

  • GenTeam is where humans and AI agents work side by side on projects in slack like channels.

  • GenOffice is our open-source AI office suite: Docs, Sheets, Slides, and PDF on Mac and Windows, with the Super Agent built in.

  • Speakly replaces typing with voice, in any app, in 50+ languages.

  • SecondBrain gives the whole system memory across your email, meetings, files, and CRM.

  • Claw is the agent that actually goes and does the work, on your machine or in the cloud.

Each product is a reason to buy, and each one is an expansion path inside your customers.

To date, we have not had a Commercial sales team selling to companies under 2,500 employees. This segment is a blank sheet. No playbook and no "this is how we do it." That's your job. We're not looking for someone who wants to run a play. We want people who want to develop it.

About the role

As a founding Mid-Market Account Executive at Genspark, you will own the full lifecycle for companies with 251 to 2,500 employees: find them, win them, and grow them. This is a full-cycle, hunter-plus-farmer seat. You are responsible for landing brand-new logos and for expanding every account you sign, driving deeper adoption, higher consumption, and multi-team upsell across our product suite.

Mid-Market at Genspark sits at the most interesting intersection in the business. Deals are large enough to matter and complex enough to require real sales craft, but fast enough that you can still close in a quarter. Clients also want both depth in the product, but offer the flexibility to adopt multiple products with a desire to consolidate where it matters. You will run multi-stakeholder cycles across a business sponsor, IT, Security, Procurement, and Legal, without the 12-month slog of true enterprise.

What you will do

  • Own the full sales cycle end to end. Prospect, qualify, demo, validate, POC, negotiate MSA and security review, close, and expand.

  • Work a mixed pipeline. You will get a portfolio patch of named accounts, and inbound trial signups will flow to you from customers who have already gotten their hands on the product. Your job is to work both hard: outbound into the patch and fast follow-up on the trials.

  • Land new logos and then grow them. Every account you sign is yours to expand: more seats, more usage, more workflows, more teams, more business units.

  • Own a consumption and expansion number alongside new business. You are measured on land and on what happens next.

  • Run multi-threaded deals with real stakeholder maps. Build champions, sell to economic buyers, and get through Security and Procurement without losing momentum.

  • Quantify value with clear ROI cases tied to real workflows: hours saved, projects unblocked, headcount leverage, revenue accelerated.

  • Partner with Solutions, Product, and Engineering on scoped POCs and technical validation. You don't have to be the deepest technical person in the room, but you do have to run the room.

  • Be the voice of the customer inside Genspark. Founding AEs shape roadmap, so bring signal, not just anecdotes.

  • Help build the MM playbook. ICP definition, account plans, deal reviews, POC frameworks, competitive positioning, expansion motion. Codify what works.

You may be a fit if

  • You have 3 to 8 years of full-cycle closing experience in SaaS or an AI sales role, with meaningful time selling into Mid-Market accounts.

  • You have a track record of consistently exceeding quota, landing net-new logos, and growing accounts materially post-sale. You can point to specific expansions you drove and how.

  • You are running agents today. Not "I've tried ChatGPT." We want to see you demo the workflow you built, walk through how it changed the way you sell, prospect, research, or run your day, and speak to what the good and bad have been. If you can't, this probably isn't the seat for you.

  • You are equally credible as a hunter and as an account owner. Neither motion is foreign to you.

  • You are experienced running multi-threaded deals across business, technical, security, procurement, and legal stakeholders.

  • You are technically fluent: comfortable in discovery with a technical buyer, comfortable in a live product conversation, comfortable talking about integrations, security posture, and data handling at a working level.

  • You have operated in an early-stage or founding-team environment before, or you are demonstrably wired for it. Ambiguity energizes you.

This role may not be a fit if

  • You need a mature playbook, mature enablement, and a fully-baked ICP on day one.

  • You want to specialize in either new logos or expansion. Here you own both.

  • Consumption-based motion, usage reviews, and joint success planning feel like someone else's job.

  • You have only sold pure Enterprise (Fortune 500, 12-month cycles) and are not excited to run a faster, more velocity-oriented motion.

  • You are not passionate about AI, or you are not willing to be a heavy Genspark user yourself.

What you get

  • A founding seat on the Commercial Sales team, with meaningful equity and the runway to grow with the function.

  • A category-defining product with real pull from the market.

  • Direct access to the Head of Scaled Revenue, product, and engineering. Short feedback loops, high leverage.

  • Competitive base, uncapped commission, accelerators, and standard benefits (health, dental, vision, 401(k), FTO).

Team: Commercial Sales, reporting to the Head of Scaled Revenue

Location: San Francisco, New York, hybrid — 3 days in office

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $115,000 – $150,000, with on-target earnings (OTE) of $230,000 – $300,000. This role is commission-eligible, with total on-target earnings structured on a 50/50 split between base salary and variable compensation, earned based on individual performance and in accordance with Company's policies. In addition to base salary, the role includes the opportunity to receive equity and a full range of benefits, including comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, flexible PTO, and 401(k).

Final compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's skills, experience, and qualifications and will be determined during the interview process. Ranges for candidates in other locations may differ based on cost of labor and other factors for those locations.

Equal Opportunity

Genspark is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

detail.title: GTM Engineer
detail.jobDescription:
About the Role

This is our founding GTM Engineer. Nothing is inherited: no legacy stack, no old playbook, no "that's how we've always done it." You get first pick of what to build, and you own the results.

The job is to build the revenue machine as software: a clean data spine, an action layer that writes safely into our CRM, ad accounts, and email, and a fleet of narrow agents that each own one motion and one number. You are not a RevOps analyst who produces dashboards and waits for someone else to implement. You are a strategist who codes.

And there's a twist most companies can't offer: every agent we run internally becomes a reference architecture we show customers. Your work won't sit in an ops backlog — it'll be on stage in sales conversations.

This role reports to the Head of GTM Engineering — flat org, no layers between you and the decision-maker.

What You'll Do

  • Build and own two to four GTM agents end to end — the loop, the evals, the guardrails, and the metric each one moves. First candidates: speed-to-lead routing, call prep, CRM hygiene from transcripts, and PQL detection from product usage.

  • Stand up the data spine — pipelines from CRM, product usage, billing, ads, and web analytics into a warehouse, with agreed definitions of CAC, pipeline, ICP fit, and PQL before any agent touches them.

  • Earn automation, don't assume it — every agent ships in propose mode with a named human approver, and graduates to auto mode only when its acceptance rate earns it.

  • Instrument everything — every agent decision logged with the data snapshot behind it, a cost-per-outcome number per agent, and a scorecard leadership can read in one screen.

  • Fix the funnel we have — lead scoring and routing, the enrichment waterfall, de-anonymizing traffic, and the handoff from self-serve to sales-assisted.

  • Turn internal wins into external assets — demos, write-ups, and talk tracks the sales and SE teams use with customers.

Who You Are

  • You've shipped a revenue system that ran in production and moved a number you can name. Clay, n8n, Python, TypeScript, SQL, or plain APIs — the tool matters less than the outcome.

  • You're fluent in SQL against a warehouse — and you know why a metric definition has to be agreed before it's automated.

  • You've lived inside a GTM org — RevOps, growth, sales engineering, or as a founder doing all three. You understand how a rep, a marketer, and a CS manager actually spend their day.

  • You build with AI agents daily — not just drafting with them. You can explain where they fail and how you catch it.

  • You write specs people can build from — a one-pager a stakeholder signs off on and a teammate can execute without a meeting.

  • You have high agency — you identify the gap and go after it. You don't need a ticket to fix something broken.

Nice to Have

  • Agent orchestration and evals experience (queues, cron, Temporal, or similar).

  • Prior work on paid acquisition loops — creative generation, bid management, kill/promote logic.

  • Deep HubSpot fluency (APIs and data model).

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $150,000 – $200,000. In addition to base salary, this role is also eligible to receive and/or earn a discretionary bonus, based on Company's plans and in accordance with Company's policies. detail.title: Account Executive, Enterprise (US)
detail.jobDescription:
Account Executive, Enterprise (US)

About Genspark

Genspark is revolutionizing the world of work with agentic AI, integrating 70+ state-of-the-art models to deliver comprehensive solutions to over a billion knowledge workers. Backed by $645M from industry-leading investors and founded by veterans from top tech companies, Genspark empowers organizations to accelerate productivity and innovation by delivering advanced AI products spanning research, documentation, presentations, coding, and more. Learn more at genspark.ai.

 

About the Role

This is a career-defining opportunity for a driven Account Executive to win and grow our largest, most strategic enterprise accounts in the US. As a key member of our Enterprise Sales team, you will own the full sales cycle with organizations of 2,500+ employees—prospecting, qualifying, demoing, solution crafting, negotiating, closing, and expanding relationships across our expanding AI suite. In this high-impact role, your work will be essential in establishing Genspark’s presence and expansion in the US enterprise market.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the entire enterprise sales process: identify, engage, and win new logos while growing footprint within existing accounts from first conversation to signed agreement and ongoing expansion.

  • Build and strategically manage a complex pipeline of large enterprise prospects, inbound interest, and named accounts.

  • Conduct in-depth discovery and solutioning with business and technical stakeholders at all levels (IC to C-Suite), mapping Genspark’s platform to complex customer needs.

  • Deliver compelling, technically credible product demonstrations and evangelize Genspark’s vision to executive audiences.

  • Drive multi-threaded enterprise deals, navigating legal, procurement, IT, and finance processes.

  • Cultivate long-term relationships, uncovering and developing cross-sell, upsell, and expansion opportunities.

  • Partner closely with Customer Success, Product, and Sales Engineering teams to ensure a seamless customer experience and create advocates within client organizations.

  • Provide feedback to marketing, product, and leadership to influence roadmap, messaging, and enablement.

 

Requirements

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying SaaS or AI enterprise sales experience, with a demonstrated track record of exceeding targets and closing seven-figure deals.

  • Proven success prospecting and landing net-new enterprise logos and driving large-scale expansions.

  • Skilled at navigating multi-stakeholder sales cycles and deeply understanding customer business drivers, technical requirements, and operational workflows.

  • Strong technical fluency: able to run end-to-end product demos and discovery conversations independently and communicate complex AI concepts to both technical and non-technical buyers.

  • Experience selling AI, analytics, workflow automation, or enterprise SaaS solutions into F1000 organizations highly preferred.

  • Entrepreneurial, highly motivated, self-directed, and comfortable thriving in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

  • Exceptional relationship builder, listener, and communicator—able to quickly establish trust and executive credibility.

  • Based in the US with ability to travel to client sites as needed.

 

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary, uncapped commission, accelerators, and equity.

  • Medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and flexible PTO.

  • Dynamic, high-growth environment with direct access to company leadership and the ability to shape sales strategy.

  • Ground-floor opportunity to build and scale a world-class enterprise sales motion at a category-defining AI company.

 

Ready to change the enterprise AI landscape? Apply now and help us power the next billion knowledge workers.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $150,000 – $180,000, with on-target earnings (OTE) of $300,000 – $360,000. This role is commission-eligible, with total on-target earnings structured on a 50/50 split between base salary and variable compensation, earned based on individual performance and in accordance with Company's policies. In addition to base salary, the role includes the opportunity to receive equity and a full range of benefits, including comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, flexible PTO, and 401(k).

Final compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's skills, experience, and qualifications and will be determined during the interview process. Ranges for candidates in other locations may differ based on cost of labor and other factors for those locations.

 

Equal Opportunity

Genspark is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.
